title: ISR-safe ring buffer with a contract you can test
objective: Implement a single-producer, single-consumer ring buffer of compile-time power-of-two capacity, with a written overflow policy, wrap-around tests, and a simulated ISR that is the only caller of push.
whyThisMatters: The first place an edge node loses data is the boundary between an interrupt (or sensor thread) and the main loop. A ring buffer with an untested overflow policy is a silent plant-floor bug.
evidence: Ring-buffer C sources with no malloc/calloc/realloc/free in that translation unit
POLICY.md naming drop-newest or drop-oldest and the exact full/empty conditions
A captured test run of wrap-around: write N+3 items into capacity N under the documented policy, then read remaining items and show the expected sequence
A captured concurrency-style test where push is called only from the simulated ISR context and pop only from main
Git history showing tests added before or with the overflow policy, not as a single final commit
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: Capacity is a compile-time power of two; a static assert or a test that fails the build rejects a non-power-of-two capacity.
After filling to capacity, the documented overflow policy is observed: POLICY.md names drop-newest or drop-oldest, and a captured test reports the count of dropped or overwritten items.
A wrap-around test writes N+3 items into a buffer of capacity N, then reads the remaining items; the captured sequence matches the policy in POLICY.md.

The ISR simulation calls push only from the simulated interrupt context and pop only from main; the test source or a comment block states that contract, and the captured run completes without a data race sanitizer report (or documents that TSan/ASan was run).
A recursive grep of the ring-buffer translation unit finds no call to malloc, calloc, realloc or free.
